sources.title: Giulia Torri, Scuola Normale Superiore: Hurrian
sources.note: Direct scholarly introduction: written attestations from late third millennium, several scribal traditions, Mittani fifteenth/fourteenth-century flourishing, later Hittite use. Map assessment independently decoded in identities.json. Not used to classify prehistoric inhabitants by language.

sources.title: Urkesh archaeological project: Royal inscriptions, Tiš-atal
sources.note: Direct scholarly edition r2, line4 pu-ur-li / purli / the temple; identifies Louvre AO19938 tablet separately from AO19937 lion and Met48.180 lion. Entry proposes Early Old Akkadian with question mark. Avoids assigning NERGAL logogram an unquestioned Hurrian divine name.

sources.title: Scuola Normale Superiore: Examples of Hurrian writing, Tišatal
sources.note: Direct institutional example dates dedication to twenty-first/twentieth centuries BCE, unlike early Old Akkadian proposal on project edition. Public wording explicitly acknowledges disputed dating. This URL and language introduction are pooled as one scholarly resource in manual budget check.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Lion foundation peg, 48.180
sources.note: Direct museum collection entry, copper alloy, circa2200 to 2100BCE, probablyTellMozan; foundation-deposit practice. Museum acquisition and proposed provenance distinguished from controlled excavation.

sources.title: Giorgio and Marilyn Kelly-Buccellati: In Search of Hurrian Urkesh (2001)
sources.note: Direct full excavation-team article, Archaeology Odyssey May/June2001, especially printed22 to 23 on sealings and site identification. Nuzi sidebar provides later Hurrian context. Excludes speculative ethnic attribution of earliest prehistoric settlement.

sources.title: Buccellati and Kelly-Buccellati: The Royal Palace and the Daughter of Naram-Sin (2000)
sources.note: Direct excavation report, Urkesh Bulletin3, printed3 to 5 daughter/seal/dynastic interpretation; printed16 roomD1 ovens andC6 toilet interpretation, brick shaft and drain. Local palace evidence only.

sources.title: Marilyn Kelly-Buccellati: Celebrating Life in Mesopotamia (2018)
sources.note: Direct Backdirt2018 article, printed59 to 62 Urkesh seals circa2250BCE; royal family, Zamena and Tuli. Distinguishes queen/royal household from ordinary population and interpretive iconography from photographed everyday action. Does not transfer Ebla/Mari anecdotes to Urkesh.

sources.title: Federico Buccellati: Perception in Palatial Architecture, Urkesh (2019)
sources.note: Direct scholarly chapter, printed37 cooking installations and proposed smoke dispersal; printed38 open drain south of palace. Avoids unsupported inference that all residents ignored smells and problematic global sewer priority claim.

sources.title: Massimo Maiocchi: A Hurrian Administrative Tablet from Third Millennium Urkesh (2011)
sources.note: Direct author preprint of ZA101pp191 to 203. Preprintpp1 to 6 context and palaeography, p6 dimensions25x27x11mm, pp7 to 10 translation and tentative taxation/filing. Recovered in secondary context; OldAkkadian attribution based on script/comparison, not clean sealed floor.

sources.title: Giorgio Buccellati: A LU E School Tablet from the Royal Palace at Urkesh (2003)
sources.note: Direct JCS55pp45 to 48: A1j1 fragments A1.69/A1.72 found1992roomB2, professions-list excerpt; apprentice scribes interpreted from floor context; contemporary Tupkish. Sumerian lexical tradition is not a Hurrian-language school text or universal schooling.

sources.title: Kharobi, Courtaud and Duday: Children at Urkesh in the Middle Bronze Age (2014)
sources.note: Direct 8ICAANE paperpp59 to 67, title An Archeothanatological Approach. Reported57tombs/63individuals aged0 to 18, 2000 to 1600BCE; age-related treatment, children in multiple burials. No infant-mortality rate, genetic kinship or clinical diagnosis inferred. Palace abandonment circa2100 followed by changing occupation.

sources.title: Marilyn Kelly-Buccellati: The Urkesh Mittani Horizon, Ceramic Evidence (2020)
sources.note: Direct scholarly chapterpp237 to 256: pp242 to 243 Mari influence/contested state-formation date, pp244 to 245 gradual Urkesh abandonment with no massive destruction attributable to Assyrian conquest. Explicitly avoids author speculative religious explanation for Assyrian choices.

sources.title: Harvard Gazette: History shines through the glass (2011)
sources.note: Direct institutional report on museum researchers and Nuzi glass/tablets; dark blue glass and possible gemstone imitation. Used solely as later second-millennium comparison beyond1500 cutoff, not as glass-invention priority or universal household possession.

proposedOverrides.summary: A broad imported label for Hurrian-speaking communities, illustrated through Urkesh and later regional connections.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Exact missing generated index ID, imported -4000 to -1500 with 3 nearly static polygons, bbox41.975 to 46.537E35.163 to 38.452N. Excludes Urkesh/TellMozan to west. Public overview explicitly explains this and prehistoric-onset problem. Broad language/cultural umbrella, not one state or ethnic map. No existing runtime Hurrian/Mittani card detected; Hittite narrative only related later comparisons. All later Mittani/Nuzi material in explicitly labelled section; no fabricated exact item years. Omit fell/successors to preserve future curated transition. Override kindregion.
